blocks.text: Imagine rolling a fair six-sided die. What is the 'average' outcome you expect over many rolls? How much do the outcomes vary from this average?

blocks.markdown: In probability and statistics, the concepts of expectation and variance help us quantify the 'average' outcome of a random process and the variability around this average. These concepts are crucial for understanding random variables and their behavior.

blocks.title: Expectation
blocks.text: The expectation (or expected value) of a discrete random variable $X$, denoted $E[X]$, is the weighted average of all possible values that $X$ can take, with weights being the probabilities of each outcome.

blocks.caption: Formula for expectation of a discrete random variable.

blocks.title: Expectation of a Fair Die Roll
blocks.prompt: Calculate the expectation of a fair six-sided die roll.

steps.text: List the possible outcomes and their probabilities. For a fair die, each outcome $x_i$ (1 through 6) has a probability $P(X = x_i) = \frac{1}{6}$.

blocks.answer: The expectation of a fair six-sided die roll is 3.5.

blocks.title: Variance
blocks.text: The variance of a random variable $X$, denoted $\text{Var}(X)$, measures the spread of its possible values. It is the expected value of the squared deviation of $X$ from its mean.

blocks.caption: Formula for variance of a discrete random variable.

blocks.title: Variance of a Fair Die Roll
blocks.prompt: Calculate the variance of a fair six-sided die roll.

steps.text: We already know $E[X] = 3.5$. Calculate $(x_i - E[X])^2$ for each outcome $x_i$.

blocks.answer: The variance of a fair six-sided die roll is approximately 2.92.

blocks.title: Standard Deviation
blocks.text: The standard deviation of a random variable $X$, denoted $\sigma_X$, is the square root of the variance. It provides a measure of spread in the same units as the random variable itself.

blocks.markdown: Standard deviation is often preferred over variance because it is in the same units as the data, making it easier to interpret.

blocks.title: Linearity of Expectation
blocks.text: The expectation of the sum of random variables is the sum of their expectations, regardless of whether the variables are independent: $E[X + Y] = E[X] + E[Y]$.

points: Expectation provides the average outcome of a random variable.
Variance measures the spread of a random variable's outcomes.
Standard deviation is the square root of variance, providing spread in the same units as the data.
Linearity of expectation holds for both independent and dependent random variables.
